newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T up on fresh tobacco settlement hopes.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T up on fresh tobacco settlement hopes.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc rose on pre-market trading on Wednesday as a press report revived hopes for a settlement of U.S. legal actions on smoking-related diseases.

A report in the Wall Street Journal said Philip Morris Cos Inc and RJR Nabisco Holdings were in secret talks with tobacco plaintiffs on a settlement that would "eliminate virtually all the industry's liability for smoking."
The newspaper said the deal would be in return for strict advertising curbs and an enormous payment that could total $300 billion over the next 25 years.
It said the two were also negotiation on behalf of B.A.T's U.S. unit Brown & Williamson.
B.A.T shares were up 14p at 527 by 0719 GMT by 0720 GMT in volume of 558,929 shares.
A B.A.T spokesman declined comment on the report, noting that any settlement would inevitably be highly price-sensitive.
"We can't confirm or deny if any talks are going on," the spokesman said.
Talk of a settlement of the growing number of U.S. court actions against tobacco firms has swirled around B.A.T shares in recent months.
The company's chief executive Martin Broughton said at the time of the company's results in March that it could be time to explore ways of settling claims because of mounting legal costs.
"We have said we will evaluate any sensible proposals made in good faith," the spokesman said.
